newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Jan open unemployment rises to 4.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Jan open unemployment rises to 4.5 pct.

text.p: Mexico's open, or base, unemployment rate rose to 4.5 percent of the economically active population during January compared to 4.1 percent in December, the National Statistics Institute said on Friday.
INEGI said in a statement the jobless rate compared to 6.4 percent unemployment during January last year.

INEGI said the rise from December to January occured most years, and that on a seasonally-adjusted basis it continued on a downward trend. The figure was better than a 4.84 percent average forecast in a Reuters survey of economists.
INEGI defines open unemployment as the percentage of the workforce older than 12 who have searched for work but have not worked more than one hour a week during a month.
The Rate of General Pressure, which measures those in work looking for a new job as well as open unemployment, was 7.9 percent in January, down from 9.7 in January 1995.

The Rate of Partial Joblessness and Unemployment, which includes open unemployment and those who have worked less than 35 hours a week due to market conditions, fell to 6.3 percent in January from 8.5 percent the same month the previous year.
The Alternative Open Unemployment Rate, which includes open unemployment as well as those who have given up looking for work, was 5.5 percent last month, down from 7.5 percent the year before.
